children: Treasury Wine's AGM commentary is seen positively at RBC despite its lack of detail. Analyst Michael Toner thinks the Australian vintner's business is tracking well even without the evidence of a quantitative trading update or guidance upgrade. Toner tells clients in a note that growth in Penfolds depletions is ahead of plan, while wholesaler depletions are also growing for the company's so-called power brands and regional heroes. On top of this, leverage seems to be falling toward Treasury Wine's FY 2028 target and the company confirmed the receipt of A$50 million in divestment proceeds. RBC has a last-published sector perform rating on the stock and a target price of 5.90 Australian dollars. Shares are up 2.2% at A$5.805. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
